text.p: The fiscal 1997 outlook for Newcor Inc is good although the first quarter could be the weakest, the company said on Thursday.
"If the economy remains stable, the outlook for fiscal 1997 is good....," said John Weinhardt, president and chief executive officer, in an earnings statement.
The company's components and assemblies segment in 1996 began producing new orders that he expected to result in "incremental sales" next year.

Weinhardt also said the company expects the first quarter 1997 to be the weakest because of the seasonal effect of the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays on the company's component and assemblies segment, and because its special machines business is at an early stage of "contracts-in-process" that will not generate strong sales and operating profit.
The company report fourth quarter earnings per share from continuing operations of $0.19 versus $0.19 from a year ago. Its current fourth quarter ended October 31.
Its shares closed unchanged at 8-1/2 on Thursday.
